description:
Somos el Equipo 1 de Astrochikis Club. Tenemos 7 años y vivimos en Ciudad Bolívar, Bogotá.

Nos encanta aprender sobre el universo, observar el cielo, hacer preguntas y descubrir cosas nuevas. Somos pequeños exploradores y tenemos una imaginación enorme.

En nuestro club aprendemos que nuestras preguntas son importantes y que podemos investigar, compartir ideas y aprender juntos.

Estamos muy emocionados de participar en NASA Space Apps Cachipay 2026. Queremos vivir una gran aventura científica, hacer nuevos descubrimientos y demostrar que, aunque somos pequeños, ¡tenemos grandes ideas!

¡Somos Astrochikis, ciudadanos del cosmos!
summary:
ROBERT-TO is a prototype Mars rover designed and built by four 7-year-old children from Astrochikis Club. Its mission is to explore the Martian surface, learn more about the planet, and investigate whether traces of microscopic life might exist there.
During the project, the children became interested in tiny organisms, drawing inspiration from tardigrades found on Earth.
To explore their questions, they designed a rover equipped with wheels, a 360-degree camera, a magnifying glass, a drill, a spectrometer, a weather station, solar panels, and a robotic arm to collect and store rock samples.
Each instrument was chosen to serve a specific purpose in the exploration process. The children researched NASA's Mars rovers, created drawings, selected materials, and built a model representing their ideas.
ROBERT-TO shows how children can turn their scientific questions into creative engineering and design solutions.
details:
What Problem Are We Trying to Solve?
This is an adaptation of the "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars". The children wanted to find out how to explore Mars, study its rocks, and better understand the conditions on its surface. One question they kept asking was whether microscopic life could exist on the planet.
Their curiosity grew as they connected what they had learned about Mars with tiny organisms found on Earth, such as tardigrades.
They did not claim that tardigrades live on Mars. Instead, they used them as an example to explore the possibility of finding tiny forms of life beyond Earth.


How Does Our Solution Work?
ROBERT-TO is a Mars exploration rover equipped with instruments selected by the children based on what they believe would be needed to investigate the planet.

  • Wheels: Would allow the rover to travel across rough and uneven terrain.
  • 360-degree camera: Would provide views of the Martian landscape in all directions.
  • Magnifying glass: Would help examine small details in rocks and soil.
  • Drill: Would extract material for sample collection.
  • Spectrometer: Would help analyze the composition of rocks and other materials.
  • Weather station: Would measure environmental conditions, such as temperature and wind.
  • Robotic sampling arm: Would collect rock samples and place them in a storage compartment.
  • Solar panels: Would provide a potential source of energy for the rover's instruments.

These instruments would not, by themselves, prove that life exists on Mars. However, they could help gather valuable information and inspire new scientific questions.


How Did We Develop Our Project?
The children began by asking their own questions and sharing their ideas.
They drew sketches of the rover, explored NASA resources, studied the features of real Mars rovers, and discussed which instruments they wanted to include.
Next, they selected materials such as cardboard, wheels, tubes, hoses, sticks, and other reusable items to bring their design to life.
Throughout the building process, they made decisions about where to place the instruments, how to represent the connections between different parts, how rock samples could be collected, and what features the rover would need to carry out its mission.


What Makes Our Solution Creative?
ROBERT-TO brings together different exploration tools in a rover designed entirely around the children's ideas.
Its creativity lies in connecting each instrument to a specific scientific task and finding ways to represent those functions using simple, accessible materials.
ROBERT-TO is a conceptual educational prototype. Its instruments represent proposed functions rather than fully operational scientific devices.


Why Is This Project Important?
This project encourages curiosity, scientific exploration, problem-solving, and teamwork.
Through this experience, the children learned that exploring another planet involves asking questions, choosing the right instruments, and understanding how each tool could contribute to a scientific investigation.
